Compounder diagnostics — non-BTS plots (interim)

Interim, biased-lede. Compounder-specific views the standard BTS does not show, on the 5,600-config gridsearch (proto-mws{N} curations, look-ahead-biased live ledes). The standard risk/return/churn plots are on the BTS page.

Anchors ['SPY', 'AGG', 'IAU', 'BIL']. Canonical (★): mws20 / cap0.333 / λ4.0 / 30d / mt0.05.

1. Does breadth buy shallower drawdowns?

Avg concurrent waves held >5% vs trailing-year giveback, coloured by cap. Lower cap forces breadth up and pushes the giveback toward zero — the compounder thesis in one plot.

2. Is breadth free? Breadth vs return

Same x-axis against annualized return. If the cloud is flat, spreading across waves costs little return; if it slopes down, breadth trades return for safety.

3. Giveback vs concentration_cap

The cap→drawdown lever directly: lower cap forces diversification and shallower full-window givebacks.

4. Trailing-year return vs giveback

The recent, forward-relevant slice (not swamped by the 2023-24 run-up), coloured by cap.

5. Canonical: concurrent breadth over time

How many distinct waves and names the canonical config actually held >5% through the window.

6. Canonical: anchor / cash weight over time

Weight the optimizer put in each safe-haven anchor. Flat-at-zero means it never went defensive on this window (the drawdowns here are rotational, not broad risk-off — why BIL stays near 0).
